name: Open/Close Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor that mounts on a door or window and reports when it opens or closes. It can switch Insteon lights or, with the Hub, send phone alerts.

productKeyVerification.note: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008) gives this category and subcategory's key to the TriggerLinc - Insteon Open / Close Sensor [2421], not to this model; that this product reports the same key is read from its sharing the identity.

steps.text: Remove the sensor cover by prying up at "open".
Install the included AA battery; don't replace the cover yet.

Peel the backing off the tape on the sensor and press it onto the door or window frame, with the SET button between the door or window edge and the battery (about 3 inches from the top on a door), so the door or window just clears it.
Press and hold the sensor's SET button for 5 seconds, until the LED starts blinking.

In the US, press and hold the SET button on the nearest Range Extender (formerly Access Point) until it beeps. If the sensor's LED keeps blinking, it is out of range: move the Range Extender closer and try again.
Peel the backing off the magnet's tape and mount the magnet within 1/2 inch of the sensor, lined up with the arrows on the sensor.
Test by opening and closing the door or window.
steps.expect: LED blinks once on each open and close

notes: The sensor is closed when the magnet is within 1/2 inch and open when it is farther.
An external contact-closure sensor (20 gauge or heavier wire) can be connected to the external sensor terminals; the sensor reads closed when either the terminals or the reed switch are closed.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.

notes: Then turn the responder on (or set it to any state) and press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED turns solid green. By default the sensor turns responders on when it opens and off when it closes.
When adding it to a Hub, the Open/Close Sensor 2843 Quick Start Guide says to press and hold the SET button until the LED blinks and then tap the SET button (the LED double-blinks).
The Open/Close Sensor is a controller only.
Older sensors with a jumper have a multi-scene mode (jumper removed): link scene 1 with the sensor open and scene 2 with it closed. Remove and reinsert the battery after changing the jumper.

verification.note: The Open/Close Sensor 2843 Owner's Manual holds the SET button 3 seconds to link responders but 5 seconds during installation. The catalog uses 3 seconds.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: While the sensor is still awake, have the Hub send extended Set (cmd1 0x2E, cmd2 0x00) with D1 0x01, D2 0x04 (stay awake) and D3 the number of seconds to stay awake.
While the device is still awake, have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's multi-linking and waking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking, Extended Set and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub. The extended Set that keeps the sensor awake is read from the Open/Close Sensor Developer Notes.

The Open/Close Sensor Developer Notes give the Link to FF Group option as bit 6 of the configuration byte, on in its default 0x43. That a link made with the SET button covers every group the sensor controls while it's on is read from that; with it off, the button links group 1 only. No document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The device sleeps to save its battery and hears messages only while awake, and no document or observation says it answers Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09); its linking steps put it in linking mode with its own controls.

The Open/Close Sensor Developer Notes give the extended Set with D1 0x01 and D2 0x04, the command set's stayAwake, with the seconds to stay awake in D3. Sending it once ALL-Linking Completed gives the device's Insteon ID, while it's still awake, is assembled from this profile's linking and waking steps; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Tap the SET button.
For each responder, set it to the scene state.
Press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to finish.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.

notes: Then press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds; the sensor's LED stops blinking and turns solid.

steps.text: While the sensor is awake, send extended Set (cmd1 0x2E, cmd2 0x00) with D1 0x01, D2 0x04 (stay awake) and D3 the number of seconds to stay awake.

notes: The Open/Close Sensor Developer Notes say the sensor sleeps quickly to save battery and must be awake to send or receive messages. Their example asks for 0xF0 seconds, about 4 minutes; the maximum is 0xFF.
The documents don't say how to wake the sensor before sending the command.

verification.note: Only the Open/Close Sensor Developer Notes cover staying awake, and they give the command but no button step to wake the sensor first.

steps.text: Unlink any responders from the sensor.
Gently remove the sensor's case with a small screwdriver.
Remove the battery.
Wait at least 15 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button while reinstalling the battery.
Release the SET button when the status LED turns on.
steps.expect: LED stays on about 4 seconds, then turns off

steps.text: Remove the sensor as a controller from each of its responders.
Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds.
Press and hold the SET button again for 3 seconds.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Subcategory 0x09 is the Door Sensor 2843-232, which has its own profile.
Its heartbeat's cmd1 is 0x11 while it's open and 0x13 while it's closed.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as about once every 24 hours; other sources give 23.8 hours.

With its jumper removed, in multi-scene mode, the sensor sends group 1 when it opens and group 2 when it closes. Later units without a jumper, as the 2016 Open/Close Sensor 2843 Owner's Manual describes them, have no multi-scene mode.
sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
